title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) Embed Differential Conservation Laws Inside Deep Learning
aiSystem: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs — Brown University / UPenn)
whyItMatters: Founded a core paradigm of scientific machine learning by encoding PDE conservation laws into neural losses—enabling mesh-free inverse physics discovery and 2025’s unstable fluid singularities.
summary: Published in Journal of Computational Physics in February 2019 (preprint November 2017) by Maziar Raissi, Paris Perdikaris, and George Em Karniadakis at Brown University and the University of Pennsylvania, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) leveraged automatic differentiation to embed nonlinear partial differential equations—such as Navier–Stokes, Schrödinger, Burgers, and Allen–Cahn equations—directly into deep neural network loss functions. Operating completely mesh-free on scattered, sparse, or noisy observations, PINNs simultaneously solved forward boundary-value PDE problems and inverse parameter-discovery problems, launching a massive scientific-ML discipline (>15,000 citations) that directly enabled DeepMind and NYU’s 2025 discovery of new unstable self-similar singularities in fluid PDEs.
technicalHighlights: Used reverse-mode automatic differentiation to enforce exact PDE residuals and boundary/initial conditions directly inside neural network training objectives.
Unified mesh-free forward PDE solving and data-driven inverse discovery of hidden physical parameters (e.g., inferring Navier–Stokes pressure fields and viscosity from sparse velocity measurements).
Directly enabled high-precision Gauss–Newton PINNs that discovered previously unknown unstable singularities in 3D Euler and IPM fluid equations in 2025.
caveats: Vanilla PINNs can suffer from spectral bias, stiff multi-scale optimization pathologies, and slower runtime than mature classical FEM/spectral solvers on clean well-posed forward PDEs, requiring specialized architectures and second-order optimizers for frontier precision.

scoreRationale.foundational: Co-founded modern Scientific Machine Learning (SciML) by unifying deep neural approximation with exact governing differential laws of physics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Cited >15,000 times across fluid mechanics, geophysics, solid mechanics, biomedicine, plasma physics, and mathematical PDE singularity discovery.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Journal of Computational Physics and independently replicated across thousands of computational-physics studies.
scoreRationale.velocity: Unlocked mesh-free inverse physics discovery from sparse experimental fields without hand-coded finite-element meshes.
